And so does Homo homini Radbruch, with his humanitarian syllogism.
I think, therefore I am. That is: I am in motion. I think, therefore I posit myself absolutely. I think, therefore I am the Absolute in motion. All of that is perfectly logical.

I think, therefore I posit myself absolutely. I posit myself absolutely, therefore I am not the “I” of the empirical self—the self that, at the very moment it thinks, is also doing other things: breathing, digesting, living in the biological sense. Instead I am another, absolute “I.” Therefore: I think, therefore I am not the empirical self. I am the abstract subject of thinking consciousness. I am.
That means: I am power. The essence of God is power. The Devil’s non-being is the will to power. The will to power is evil. Power is good. A simple litany for simple individuals.
On the Jürgen Habermas campaign against Heidegger in the summer of 1953: Theodor Wiesengrund Adorno’s Minima Moralia says, word for word, on p. 365 (the passage dates from 1935):

“If the bourgeois class has, since time immemorial, cherished the dream of a savage Volksgemeinschaft—a community in which everyone suppresses everyone else—then children already bearing first names like Horst and Jürgen, and surnames like Bergenroth, Bojunga, and Eckhardt, acted out (sic) that dream before the adults were historically mature enough to make it a reality.”
Bravo! And Jürgen Habermas was the given, predestined name for the Haberfeld-style public shaming campaign against Martin Heidegger.
(On Petwaidic and Bourdin): The elite are those whose sociology no one dares to write.

Every name is a Nahme—a taking.
God is power—and direct power at that: potestas directa.
The Devil is the will to power.
The will to power: the ideology of professional revolutionaries and émigrés; indirect power, potestas indirecta.

Woe to us when they seize power—that is, when they are finally able to take revenge. For revenge is really the only thing they are capable of. See the Federal Constitutional Court’s judgment of 17 December 1953.

So enough of that! Carry your uncomprehended heart to the dead! Stop letting yourself be invited, only to be uninvited again. Stop letting yourself be spat on by windbag intellectuals like Moritz Bonn, and recognize your own Νόμος—your own Nomos!
God is dead. That means: he is no longer present; he is absent.
There is no God other than the God who is present—the tutela praesens, the protection that is here with us.
To someone listening to the radio, anything that is not speaking at that particular moment is absent.
God is good: that means direct power is good. It gives effective protection, and such protection comes from him alone.
But potestas indirecta, indirect power, is evil. It is on the left—izquierda. It is not present; it is not even represented.

Bonald said: society itself—la société, hence socialism! –––– That means socialism!—cannot declare its belief in God, because society itself, by the very fact of existing, already implicitly contains and presupposes the “presence of God.”
On this, Robert Spaemann writes (“The Error of the Traditionalist,” Wort und Wahrheit, no. 7, July 1953):
“The concept of presence, as distinct from the mere existence of God, is, incidentally, a very profound one. It prepares us to understand Nietzsche’s ‘God is dead.’”
Yes, Robert Spaemann. That is it. And this remark of yours really is a very profound one.
“A God who is not present is as good as dead.”
Partir, c’est un peu mourir—to leave is to die a little.
Socialism wants to make God present.
It does so through universal and equal participation: participation in Leviathan itself—the magnus homo, the great man—but also in Leviathan’s banquet.
Hegel: the state is God made present.
Marx: the state must be slaughtered for the banquet of Leviathan.
That is the great sacrament of Marxist socialism. It was performed long ago, over there in Russia.
People used to say—the old kitsch word—tableau. Today they say: situation.

Here in the West, the other sacrament—the sacrament of wine—was destroyed long ago. The Coal and Steel Community will canalize the Moselle; Moselle wine will be canalized along with it. The Moselle winegrowers will become members of an association of <alcohol-free> fruit-juice processors. The cardinals will have to give it their blessing. After all, they took the wine away from the laity long ago. Tacito rumore Mosella—the Moselle with its quiet murmur; that is, of course, the Moselle before it has been canalized.
They strum the devastation on harps, And trumpet the Last Judgment. They fiddle away at indignation, And play our nothingness on harpsichords. (Rilke)

Wine is no longer a sacrament today. Aldous Huxley recommends mescaline instead. But some magnificent remnants of wine still survive. Let us drink them before the Moselle is canalized and France is integrated. Let us drink these beautiful remnants!
Now and then each man took the best; I shall hold fast to these beautiful remnants.

How does an islander, living out of his maritime existence, come to recommend foreign intoxicating drugs when he has probably not tasted even the smallest fraction of Europe’s wonderful wines? I ought to write to Der Spiegel, which discusses Huxley’s discovery without protest (March 1954): Why are you spreading false teachings that help uproot today’s Europeans from place? But there is no point protesting anymore. They would only think it was a joke.

That is a natural wish. It can keep even an old man standing for quite a long time, and hold him firmly on this earth.

Anni said: “I know my Pappenheimers.” I replied: “Then you know something old-fashioned. I know my Oppenheimers.” On 19 July 1954, Heinz Weitzel of Frankfurt told me: “I have been saying that for a long time.” So apparently the thought is an obvious one—and concretely true.

To one particular persecutor of mine, whom I believe to be honest: Why are you persecuting me? My situation is very close to yours. We are jumping from one ice floe to another, and it is childish of you to imagine that your ice floe is somehow more permanent than the one I happen to be drifting on at the moment. I know perfectly well that you do not really believe this either. But instead of recognizing how similar our situations are, you appeal to the owners of the ice floe on which you happen to stand.
